Getting started with varm

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

What is implemented

This table was compiled from the package source (R/, src/*.cpp), not from the package description. Items marked “not yet” appear in the DESCRIPTION, _pkgdown.yml or notes but have no code.

Area Implemented Entry point
Reduced-form VAR OLS with constant, linear trend, exogenous regressors; lag selection (AIC, HQ, SC, FPE); summary, coef, resid, fitted, vcov, logLik; companion-matrix stability varm(), var_select(), stability()
Uncertainty residual bootstrap, wild bootstrap (Rademacher, Mammen), asymptotic Monte Carlo, Kilian bias correction draws(), irf(ci = )
Dynamics IRFs (with bands, normalisation, cumulation), FEVD, historical decomposition, forecasts with bands irf(), fevd(), hd(), forecast()
SVAR identification Cholesky, Blanchard-Quah long-run, sign restrictions (Haar rotations), user-supplied impact matrix id_chol(), id_longrun(), id_sign(), id_given()
Bayesian VAR conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart with Minnesota, sum-of-coefficients and single-unit-root priors; exact sampling for fixed hyperparameters, Metropolis for hierarchical hyperparameters bvarm(), prior_minnesota()
Proxy SVAR varm_proxy(), varm_proxy_robust()
Not yet heteroskedasticity identification, narrative/zero restrictions, stochastic volatility, shrinkage (SSVS) priors, TVP-VAR, FAVAR, local projections, data simulation helper

The _pkgdown.yml reference index also lists favar, autoplot.varm, autolayer.varm and sim_var; none of these exist in the code.

Data

yraw holds three quarterly US series (columns X1-X3: inflation, unemployment and the interest rate in the Koop-Korobilis data set). We rename them and drop the tibble class.

y <- as.matrix(yraw)
colnames(y) <- c("inflation", "unemployment", "rate")
y <- ts(y, start = 1953, frequency = 4)
dim(y)
#> [1] 215   3

Lag selection and estimation 

var_select(y, pmax = 6)$selection
#> AIC  HQ  SC FPE 
#>   6   2   2   6
fit <- varm(y, p = 2)
fit
#> <varm> VAR(2) with 3 variables, 213 effective observations
#> logLik = -338.416; max |eigenvalue| = 0.946

coef(fit) returns the (Kp + d) x K coefficient matrix (lags first, then deterministic terms); lag_matrices(fit) returns the K x K x p array of lag matrices.

round(lag_matrices(fit)[, , 1], 3)
#>              inflation unemployment   rate
#> inflation        1.538       -0.281 -0.057
#> unemployment    -0.010        1.330 -0.021
#> rate             0.546       -0.647  0.777

Impulse responses

irf() defaults to a Cholesky identification and a residual bootstrap. The result stores the point estimate in $estimate (response x shock x horizon) and bands in $bands.

ir <- irf(fit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16, nboot = 300)
ir
#> <varm IRF> K = 3, horizon 0..16, id = chol, bands: 68%/90%
dim(ir$estimate)
#> [1]  3  3 17

Use ci = "none" for point estimates only, or "wild", "wild_mammen", "mc" for the other draw generators. normalise rescales a shock (here a unit shock to the rate), and cumulative accumulates responses of variables entered in differences.

ir_wild <- irf(fit, horizon = 16, ci = "wild", nboot = 300,
               normalise = list(shock = "rate", variable = "rate", size = 1))

Plotting

plot() on an IRF or FEVD object draws a response-by-shock grid. The return value depends on the installed version (base graphics or ggplot2), so the code below only calls plot() and the optional subsetting arguments.

plot(ir, shocks = "rate")

as.data.frame() gives a tidy table for your own plots.

head(as.data.frame(ir), 4)
#>       response        shock h    estimate       q0.05       q0.16     q0.84
#> 1    inflation    inflation 0  0.30781926  0.27765004  0.28929732 0.3223588
#> 2 unemployment    inflation 0 -0.01166515 -0.05059755 -0.03438827 0.0181515
#> 3         rate    inflation 0  0.08772352 -0.02916307  0.01785599 0.1621194
#> 4    inflation unemployment 0  0.00000000  0.00000000  0.00000000 0.0000000
#>        q0.95
#> 1 0.33550192
#> 2 0.03408146
#> 3 0.20774654
#> 4 0.00000000

FEVD, historical decomposition and forecasts 

fv <- fevd(fit, horizon = 12, ci = "none")
round(fv$estimate[, , 13], 3)    # response x shock at horizon 12
#>               shock
#> response       inflation unemployment  rate
#>   inflation        0.825        0.161 0.014
#>   unemployment     0.174        0.792 0.034
#>   rate             0.349        0.274 0.377
h <- hd(fit)
dim(h$contributions)             # time x variable x shock
#> [1] 213   3   3
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 8, nboot = 300)
fc
#> <varm forecast> h = 8
#>      inflation unemployment   rate
#> [1,]    2.7209       4.9214 4.6197
#> [2,]    2.6572       5.0522 4.4527
#> [3,]    2.6436       5.1565 4.3276
#> [4,]    2.6558       5.2322 4.2508
#> [5,]    2.6821       5.2834 4.2096
#> [6,]    2.7173       5.3164 4.1951
#> [7,]    2.7582       5.3374 4.1993
#> [8,]    2.8028       5.3513 4.2163
dim(fc$bands)                    # horizon x variable x probability
#> [1] 8 3 4
